title: Identification of $i^!$ with sections with support
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of $k$-schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, with the pulled-back condensed module-object coefficients and bounded constructible categories $\Dbc(-,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Write $\mathcal C_T=\Loc(\Dbc(T,\Lambda))$ for the full localizing subcategory of the ambient unbounded category $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]; here $\Dbc=\Dctf$ by [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]. Let $i^!:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Z$ be the right adjoint of $Ri_!=i_*$ on these localizing categories [sk-prop-sf-existence], with the closed-immersion normalization $Ri_!=i_*$ understood as part of this adjunction. Let $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ be the derived sections-with-support functor of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]. For every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ there is an isomorphism
$$i^!K\simeq R\underline\Gamma_ZK$$
in $\mathcal C_Z$, natural in $K$ and compatible with the counits $i_*i^!K\to K$ and $i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\to K$.

proof.text: Put $H_K=i^!K$ and $S_K=R\underline\Gamma_ZK$. The field-coefficient equality $\Dctf=\Dbc$ in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] identifies the localizing categories in the statement with those in [sk-prop-sf-existence]. The generating-subcategory containment in [sk-def-localizing-closure] gives $K\in\mathcal C_X$, so the adjoint is defined on $K$ and $H_K\in\mathcal C_Z$. By [det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-support], $S_K\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$, hence $S_K\in\mathcal C_Z$. By [sk-def-localizing-closure], the categories $\mathcal C_Z,\mathcal C_X$ are full subcategories of the ambient unbounded module-object derived categories. In particular all the Hom sets involving their objects below are the ambient Hom sets.

source.place: First sentence and the sentence identifying the full localizing subcategories.

proof.text:
For $A\in\mathcal C_Z$, use the stipulated adjunction $i_*\dashv i^!$ of [sk-prop-sf-existence] and the ambient adjunction $i_*\dashv R\underline\Gamma_Z$ of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support](1). With their counits denoted by $\varepsilon^!_K$ and $\varepsilon^S_K$, respectively, these give bijections
$$\alpha_{A,K}:\Hom_{\mathcal C_Z}(A,H_K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{D(X)}(i_*A,K),\quad a\longmapsto\varepsilon^!_K\circ i_*(a),$$
$$\beta_{A,K}:\Hom_{\mathcal C_Z}(A,S_K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{D(X)}(i_*A,K),\quad b\longmapsto\varepsilon^S_K\circ i_*(b).$$
The first uses $i_*A\in\mathcal C_X$, supplied by the lower-shriek functor on the localizing categories; the second is valid for every ambient $A$, so in particular for this one. Fullness from step 1 identifies the indicated groups exactly. Both bijections are natural in $A$ and in bounded constructible $K$, because they are adjunction bijections. Consequently $\tau_{A,K}=\beta_{A,K}^{-1}\alpha_{A,K}$ and its inverse form mutually inverse natural transformations $h_{H_K}\leftrightarrows h_{S_K}$ on $\mathcal C_Z$.

source.place: The two adjunction Hom bijections and their identification using fullness.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in $\mathcal C_Z$ to $\tau_{-,K}$ and its inverse. It gives unique maps $\theta_K:H_K\to S_K$ and $\rho_K:S_K\to H_K$ whose postcomposition transformations are these two transformations; explicitly $\theta_K=\tau_{H_K,K}(1_{H_K})$. Since the transformations are mutually inverse, the injectivity in that same Yoneda statement gives $\rho_K\theta_K=1_{H_K}$ and $\theta_K\rho_K=1_{S_K}$. Thus $\theta_K$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal C_Z$. Evaluating $\beta\tau=\alpha$ at $A=H_K$ and $1_{H_K}$ gives
$$\varepsilon^S_K\circ i_*(\theta_K)=\varepsilon^!_K.$$
Any map satisfying this equality has the same image under the bijection $\beta_{H_K,K}$, hence equals $\theta_K$. This proves the asserted counit compatibility, including uniqueness for the specified adjunctions.

source.place: Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda: full faithfulness and evaluation at the identity; applied to the two representations in the blueprint proof.

proof.text: Let $q:K\to K'$ be a morphism of bounded constructible complexes. The two maps $S(q)\circ\theta_K$ and $\theta_{K'}\circ i^!(q)$ from $H_K$ to $S_{K'}$ have the same image under $\beta_{H_K,K'}$: by naturality of the support counit in [sk-lem-formal-closed-support](1), the first has image $q\circ\varepsilon^S_K\circ i_*\theta_K=q\circ\varepsilon^!_K$; by naturality of the exceptional counit in [sk-prop-sf-existence], the second has image $\varepsilon^!_{K'}\circ i_*i^!(q)=q\circ\varepsilon^!_K$. Injectivity of $\beta_{H_K,K'}$ makes these maps equal. Hence the isomorphism is natural in $K$. For the final constructibility consequence, [sk-def-sfb-constructible] defines $\Dbc$ by bounded constructible cohomology. Each $H^n(\theta_K)$ is an isomorphism, so $H^n(i^!K)$ vanishes whenever $H^n(S_K)$ does and is constructible whenever $H^n(S_K)$ is. Since $S_K\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$ by step 1, this gives $i^!K\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Final sentence: uniqueness makes the comparison natural in K; the two transposes are written out.
